criteria.objective_evidence: Workings for each sampled trade
criteria.fail_examples: Size above the risk rule

criteria.description: Correlated exposure is grouped and capped
criteria.objective_evidence: Group list and cap check
criteria.fail_examples: Treating correlated names as independent

criteria.description: Drawdown ladder and no-trade gates are followed
criteria.objective_evidence: Account path versus the written rungs, including any no-trade days
criteria.fail_examples: Trading through a halt; revenge sizing

criteria.description: Gaps and events are stress-tested
criteria.objective_evidence: Event calendar checks and a gap multiple on overnight or event trades
criteria.fail_examples: Holding leverage into an unplanned binary event

criteria.description: Arrival versus fill and costs are recorded
criteria.objective_evidence: Journal fields for arrival, fill and itemised costs
criteria.fail_examples: Mid-price reporting presented as a fill

criteria.description: Stops are set before entry and not widened
criteria.objective_evidence: Pre-trade stop in the journal matching the working
criteria.fail_examples: Moving a stop further from entry after entry

criteria.description: Losing-streak, revenge, overconfidence and no-trade rules are evidenced when they fire
criteria.objective_evidence: The written plan or final review states the precommitment. Journal notes are required when a gate actually fired, including a documented no-trade decision. If no gate fired in the 30 trades, the written rule itself is the evidence; the learner is not failed for an uneventful sample
criteria.fail_examples: Doubling size after losses to get back to even; taking a trade after a written cooling-off gate

criteria.description: AI-generated market claims are checked; any uploaded strategy is restated and cannot bypass rails
criteria.objective_evidence: A fact-check of one AI-generated market claim against a primary source (this satisfies the written exercise). An uploaded strategy is not required. If one is present: a paraphrase of what the AI understood, a paper-test note, and a reject/approve status that preserves risk limits
criteria.fail_examples: Using an unsourced AI statistic as evidence; approving a prompt that bypasses stops or recovery-sizes after losses

criteria.description: Human-school evidence is not substituted for AI-strategy approval or the reverse
criteria.objective_evidence: The capstone journal is labelled as the human-school paper process. If no strategy was uploaded, that label alone meets this criterion. If an upload is present, it is labelled separately and is not used to mark the school complete
criteria.fail_examples: Presenting an uploaded-strategy backtest as the human capstone; claiming course completion automatically approves an upload

criteria.description: The best argument against each trade is stated
criteria.objective_evidence: A counter-evidence field on sampled journals
criteria.fail_examples: Empty counter-evidence fields

criteria.description: Decision quality is separated from outcome
criteria.objective_evidence: A review that discusses rule adherence independently of P&L
criteria.fail_examples: Judging the plan solely by whether the sample made money

criteria.description: Rules were fixed before the tested sample where claimed
criteria.objective_evidence: A dated plan or parameter freeze
criteria.fail_examples: Changing rules after seeing the result and presenting them as prior

criteria.description: Net, complete, paper-labelled reporting with no accreditation claim
criteria.objective_evidence: A final statement that completion is general education, not a qualification, profit guarantee, or live-competence certificate
criteria.fail_examples: Presenting paper marks as live skill or as industry accreditation

practical_rubric.alignment_note: The official capstone scoring list remains the ten named capstone criteria. The three additional module fields (psychology_precommitment, ai_skill_approval, separate_tracks) are evidenced from the written plan, the required AI claim fact-check, and optional uploads; they are not a parallel hidden 13-item exam and an upload is not required to pass.

content_review.note: All 287 question stems, keys and option rationales were read for conceptual correctness. Practical prompts were compared with their rubrics and the capstone list. High-risk lessons were read in full; remaining lessons were claim-scanned. This is not a substitute for a market practitioner, educator, lawyer or compliance reviewer. Do not imply that every sentence is covered by the evidence register.

learning_tracks.human_school: Lessons, quizzes, paper exercises, journals and the Module 21 capstone.
learning_tracks.ai_upload_skills: Uploaded or described strategies: restatement of what the AI understood, paper test with costs, versioning, results and approval status. Uploads must never bypass written risk limits.
learning_tracks.separation: The two tracks are recorded separately. A quiz score does not approve an upload, and an uploaded backtest does not complete the school.
